title: David Arquette
summary: Episode 60 combines two different programs. In the first, David Arquette joins a post-Dodgers-game conversation about the separate KGB graffiti histories, Robbie Conal's political posters, money as a vehicle for care, violence and creativity, Las Vegas, Choe's earlier Subliminal Projects show, a Sizzler birthday gathering, Paul Reubens, and Upper Playground. After the guest segment ends, Critter performs an extended solo interview with unheard or imaginary questions about childhood, concussions, San Francisco, hockey, music, intimacy, camping, and the Raiders. The archive must distinguish the two KGB expansions, treat recollections as claims, correct medical and etymological misinformation, protect childhood and third-party identities, and resist converting contextual speaker familiarity into unvalidated named turns.
sensitivity: Racial and ethnic slurs; Holocaust and Hitler discussion; violence and childhood abuse; explicit sexual content; gambling and addiction; angina and concussion disclosures; minors' sexual history; misogyny and racial stereotyping; private residence and travel patterns; third-party body and pregnancy commentary.
speaker_policy: No named dialogue is publishable. Episode 60 currently contains zero diarized turns and zero voice windows, and the independent held-out attribution gate has not passed. David Arquette's guest presence and Critter's solo-host framing are contextually supported, but names below identify subjects and segment roles rather than acoustically validated utterances.
